messages:
Jamie: Thinking through an edge case for the Console experiment flow — we want to support per-variant traffic priority (so teams can mark a variant as higher precedence) + per-variant per-user QPS caps. Question: when a high-priority variant is rate-limited for a user, should routing fallback to the next priority variant, or go straight to the service default model? :thinking:
Rae: UI point — we need to show `priority` and `per_user_qps` fields in the variant creation form. Also warn if someone sets identical priorities across >1 variant without weights. :eyes:
Marco: Backend thought: fallback to next priority variant seems sensible (deterministic), but we must record a `fallback_reason` in telemetry (`quota_exhausted`, `variant_unavailable`, etc.). Otherwise ops can't tell why traffic moved.
Priya: From product POV: fallback-to-next-priority is fine, but add an `isolation` flag on variant — if true, do NOT fallback, instead route to service default (fail open) and alert. Use-case: sensitive experiments that must not contaminate other variants.
Luis: Implementation note: per-user token buckets live in redis already for global rate limits. We can namespace token buckets per `experiment_id:variant_id:user_id`. That should perform. API fields: `variant_priority: int`, `max_qps_per_user: float|null`, `isolation: bool` (default false). DB migration required.
Rae: For the Console UX, proposal for the variant row: show small badge `P3` / `P2` and an inline tooltip: "priority decides fallback order; lower number = higher priority". If `max_qps_per_user` is set, show a tiny alert icon that opens a modal explaining quota semantics.
Marco: Example routing algorithm sketch:
``` 
# pseudocode
ordered = variants.sorted_by(priority asc, created_at asc)
for v in ordered:
  if v.isolation and v.user_quota_exhausted(user):
    return service_default
  if not v.user_quota_exhausted(user) and v.has_capacity():
    return v
# none matched -> return service_default
```
Rae: Nice. Also UI needs to surface conflicts: e.g., two variants both `P1` with overlapping audiences. Show a preflight validation screen.
Priya: Telemetry ask: in rollout dashboard add a small waterfall that shows traffic split after fallback. Metrics: `requests_by_path` (variant->fallback->default), `fallback_rate`, and latency per path. This will help detect regression when fallback increases.
Jamie: Good point — add an early-warning alert when `fallback_rate > 5%` over 10m for production experiments.
Luis: Migration notes: add columns to `experiment_variants` table: `priority int default 1000`, `max_qps_per_user float null`, `isolation boolean default false`. Backfill existing variants with `priority=1000` (low precedence). Watch out for index size (we'll use smallint if needed).
Marco: We'll need to extend the router API: `POST /route` should include `user_id` (optional) so server can honor per-user caps. Also add `fallback_chain` to response metadata for debugging.
Rae: UX deliverables: form fields + validation + preflight modal + dashboard badge. Keeping it compact.
Priya: MVP scope suggestion: 1) backend routing + telemetry + small routing API change, 2) Console: show priority + validation warnings, 3) dashboard: basic fallback_rate metric. Defer `isolation` toggle to follow-up unless legal demands it.
Jamie: Sounds good. I'll open a short RFC and attach the pseudocode + DB changes. Action items: Marco backend ticket, Rae UI ticket, Luis infra ticket for redis namespacing, Priya to add acceptance criteria.
deploy-bot: patch deployed to staging cluster for variant-priority router (canary). :rocket:
